Jordan (Acme): hey team — around 2027-03-10T14:12:09Z we started seeing lots of 429s from /v1/jobs and multiple jobs getting created twice. Billing spiked. attaching minimal repro and logs below. can you advise immediate mitigations?

Jordan (Acme): logs: ```
[2027-03-10T14:12:08.123Z] request_id=rc-abc123 status=429 Retry-After=1 x-rate-limit-remaining=0 x-rate-limit-reset=27
[2027-03-10T14:12:08.987Z] SDK retry attempt=1 request_id=rc-def456 status=201 job_id=job-789
[2027-03-10T14:12:09.512Z] SDK retry attempt=2 request_id=rc-ghi789 status=201 job_id=job-790
```

Jordan (Acme): sample client snippet (we're on sdk-js v2.2.1): ```js
const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.RW_KEY });
await client.jobs.create({ payload }, { retry: undefined }); // using defaults
```

Alicia (support): thanks — can you confirm: 1) exact SDK version (you said v2.2.1), 2) are you sending Idempotency-Key header on POST /v1/jobs, 3) do you see Retry-After headers consistently? Also share one request_id for one duplicated pair.

Jordan (Acme): confirmed v2.2.1, we don't set Idempotency-Key (legacy code). Retry-After present sometimes (1-3s). request_ids: rc-abc123 -> rc-def456 are the two that map to duplicate results.

Sam (sdk): ping — on v2.2.x the JS SDK had relatively aggressive retry behavior: default max_retries=6, base_delay~200ms, no full jitter, and crucially it would retry POSTs even without Idempotency-Key. That combination can produce a retry storm (esp. with 100+ parallel clients). In v2.3 we changed defaults: max_retries=4, strategy=exponential with full jitter, and we do NOT retry non-idempotent POSTs unless an Idempotency-Key is present.

Sam (sdk): immediate recommendations:
- patch your client to set an Idempotency-Key for create endpoints (uuid per logical operation)
- or lower/disable client retries while you investigate (set maxRetries=0)
- respect server Retry-After header (sdk has respectRetryAfter flag)

Sam (sdk): example config to harden quickly: ```js
const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: RW_KEY, retry: { maxRetries: 3, strategy: 'full-jitter', baseDelayMs: 200, maxDelayMs: 4000, respectRetryAfter: true } });
await client.jobs.create(body, { headers: { 'Idempotency-Key': uuidv4() } });
```

Jordan (Acme): what's the fastest way to stop duplicates right now? rollback to v2.1? disable retries?

Alicia (support): fastest: set maxRetries=0 in your runtime config and deploy that change — that'll stop client retries immediately. If you use a feature flag or config service, toggle it. Also add Idempotency-Key on the next deploy so future retries are safe. We can also temporarily increase your quota for a short window if you need throughput.

Matt (sre): adding context from infra: our rate limiter is a token-bucket with a short burst window. Typical bucket size = 500 tokens and refill rate aligned to the reserved capacity. With many parallel clients that retry without jitter, you can exhaust the bucket and then clients will continually see 429 and retry in sync -> amplified load. Two notes: 1) always respect Retry-After header returned by server (it gives a cooldown in seconds), 2) client-side token/leaky-bucket throttle avoids synchronized retries.

Matt (sre): pseudo leaky-bucket client pattern: ```
let tokens = capacity; // e.g. 50
function allow() { if (tokens > 0) { tokens--; return true } return false }
setInterval(() => { tokens = Math.min(tokens + refill, capacity) }, 1000)
// call allow() before sending request, otherwise queue
```

Sam (sdk): also important: treat 401/403/402 differently — don't retry automatically on auth or billing errors. The SDK will not retry on 402 and will surface the error so callers can surface billing to users. For 401/403, refresh token flow should be invoked and then retry once after a successful refresh. For 429/5xx, use exponential backoff + full jitter, respect Retry-After header precedence over exponential schedule.

Sam (sdk): config note: v2.2.1 behavior you saw is the main cause. We can replicate locally if you share a small repro (we have a dev harness that simulates token buckets).

deploy-bot: deploy finished "rate-limiter/experiment-2027-03-10" at 2027-03-10T14:11:40Z — rolling config change to soften hard caps for a subset of clients (id: rl-exp-42) :rocket:

Jordan (Acme): ok patching now to set maxRetries=0 and plumb Idempotency-Key. will report back in ~10m. thanks.

Rachael (cs): Rachael here — I'll open a billing review ticket for the spike. Jordan please DM me the list of request_ids + approximate token/units consumed and time window. We'll review credits for accidental duplicates.

Alicia (support): next steps we have: 1) Jordan to deploy temporary no-retry patch (maxRetries=0) + add Idempotency-Key in next deploy, 2) Jordan to send list of request_ids to Rachael for billing review, 3) Sam to help reproduce in SDK harness and produce an advisory note (we should update docs & release notes), 4) Matt to verify server-side metrics for the burst experiment. Thanks all :thumbsup:

Jordan (Acme): thanks — will follow up with request ids and rollout status.
